name: Similarweb
summary: Competitive intelligence on web traffic, search and ads — what your competitors' visitors do.
best_for: a single analyst or marketer who needs competitor traffic and channel estimates often enough to justify $125 a month, and teams who are prepared to negotiate an annual contract for more than one seat
skip_if: you want a quick check on one competitor — the free tier and public estimates cover that, and the cheapest paid plan is $125 a month for a single user
honest_knock: Similarweb does publish a price — $125 a month for one seat on annual billing, or $199 if you pay monthly. What it does not publish is anything above one seat: the business and enterprise tab carries no figure at all and routes straight to a sales call, where the number depends on what they think you can pay. So the decision splits in two. One analyst can price this today and start a trial without speaking to anyone. A team walks into a negotiation, and should walk in with a ceiling already written down — plus the two line items priced apart from the seats: 37 months of data history is an add-on, and API access is quoted separately.

pricing.entry_price_terms: per month on annual billing ($199 monthly) for one user
pricing.notes: (re-verified 2026-10-16 on their own pricing page; first read 2026-08-25) The entrepreneur plans are published: $125 per month on annual billing for Competitive Intelligence, $333 for Competitive Intel & SEO & AEO, and $542 for Competitive Intel, SEO & AEO & Ads — or $199, $399 and $649 respectively on monthly billing, each for a single user. Included history differs by plan and is easy to miss: 3 months on the entry plan, 6 months on the two above it. What is not published is the business and enterprise tab: it carries no figure at all and routes every tier to 'Talk to sales' for a custom package, and the FAQ repeats that premium features require one. A free trial is offered without a stated length. Up to 37 months of data history is sold as an add-on rather than an inclusion, and API access is either standalone or inside a custom package.

vendor_mcp.what: Hosted server at mcp.similarweb.com: website and keyword analysis, app-market data across iOS and Android, Amazon seller and product data, and lead enrichment from digital behaviour.
vendor_mcp.plan: Stated plainly: a "Similarweb subscription with API access: API-only, Business, or Enterprise plans", plus an active API key from your account settings. Metered too — "MCP uses the same data credits as standard API calls", and a chattier agent that pulls several endpoints spends more of them.
